transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
Since my husband died, it feels like this heavy sadness never lifts, like I’m stuck under it and can’t find any joy in anything anymore. I just feel so completely empty and exhausted all the time.

Before your husband died, had you ever had another period lasting at least two weeks when you felt this depressed or lost interest in things most of the day nearly every day? Or is this the first time you’ve ever felt this way?

No, this is the very first time I have ever felt this kind of deep sadness or lost interest in my life. Before my husband passed away, we lived a very quiet, orderly, and stable life, and I never struggled with anything like this.

Do these feelings come mainly in waves when you think about or are reminded of your husband, or are you feeling depressed and unable to enjoy anything most of the day nearly every day no matter what is happening around you?

It isn't in waves; it is a constant, heavy presence every single day. I wake up every morning feeling like there is a concrete block on my chest, and the gray fog just never lifts. No matter what is happening around me, I can't find a single spark of joy or interest in anything anymore.
Have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty about yourself, beyond just missing your husband? Or do your thoughts stay mostly focused on the loss itself?

Yes, the guilt is overwhelming and goes far beyond just missing him. I spend hours every day obsessing over my past mistakes, convinced that I was a fundamentally bad wife who poisoned our marriage. I honestly feel like his death is a punishment for my shortcomings, and that I don't deserve to be here.
Have you had thoughts of wanting to die or of killing yourself? If so, have you thought about how you would do it or made any plans?

Yes, almost every day I catch myself thinking it would be better for everyone if I just didn't wake up. On my worst days, I've gone as far as sitting in my car in the garage picturing letting it run, though I haven't actually done it. It really scares me that my mind even goes there.

final_diagnosis.reason: First lifetime episode of a major depressive episode with severe intensity: persistent depressed mood and marked anhedonia nearly every day, excessive guilt/worthlessness beyond bereavement-focused thoughts, profound exhaustion, and recurrent suicidal ideation with method imagery. Symptoms are described as pervasive rather than occurring in grief waves after the husband's death, supporting a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms rather than normal grief alone.
